summary: A convention without living justification that misdirects agents and perpetuates bad practice

meta.heuristic: If a convention fights the tool default, suspect it. If it causes friction twice, scrape it.
meta.usage: The capitalized Justfile rule is a barnacle — no living justification, creates recurring friction.

summary: A self-contained project directory with named compartments, each carrying a single responsibility

meta.heuristic: If it accumulates files, it gets an index. If it has an index, it gets a justfile group.
meta.usage: This repo is a silo: briefs, debriefs, decisions, playbooks, docs, src, scripts, tests.

summary: A thin delegation layer that routes to real implementations; never the workbench

meta.heuristic: The justfile is a facade, not a workbench. Complex logic lives in scripts.
meta.usage: The justfile delegates to TypeScript scripts; it does not contain inline bash.

summary: Prove patterns in scripts/lab/ before touching production code

meta.heuristic: Never experiment in production paths. The lab is the proving ground.
meta.usage: We proved the PID file pattern in scripts/lab/pid-file.ts before building server-lifecycle.ts.

summary: The act of removing a barnacle: deleting the convention, updating docs, recording the removal

meta.heuristic: Scrape is the verb for barnacle removal. Document the scrape so it does not return.
meta.usage: We scraped the capitalized Justfile convention and recorded it in the conventions playbook.

summary: Break cross-directory couplings before moving directories in a restructure

meta.heuristic: Phase 0: extract shared modules. Phase 1: move directories. Phase 2: update references.
meta.usage: We extracted db.ts and trade-calculator.ts to src/lib/ before moving server/ to src/server/.

summary: Small change, check, commit or revert. Never pile fixes on a broken state.

meta.heuristic: Make small change → check → commit or revert. If stuck >15 min: stop, revert, ask.
meta.usage: We extracted push logic to a script, checked, committed. When check failed, we reverted.

summary: The silent divergence between a document index and the filesystem it describes

meta.heuristic: Indexes rot because files are added/deleted but indexes are not updated. reg-sync detects this.
meta.usage: The debriefs index had 3 missing files until reg-sync surfaced the drift.

summary: A single JSONL schema used by all document indexes in a silo

meta.heuristic: One schema: { file, date, status, summary, meta? }. No special cases. New registries slot in without tool changes.
meta.usage: All five indexes (briefs, debriefs, decisions, playbooks, docs) use the unified schema.

summary: The accumulation of unstructured, chaotic information that defeats comprehension

meta.heuristic: The primary cognitive function is mentation: transforming stuff into things.
meta.usage: A 683-line justfile with inline bash is conceptual entropy. Extract to scripts.

summary: The transformation of unstructured inputs (stuff) into structured, actionable outputs (things)

meta.heuristic: Map vs territory. Outputs are maps. Operate with mentational humility.
meta.usage: Building the unified registry was mentation: four chaotic schemas became one.

summary: Simulated bias-check before answering complex queries

meta.heuristic: Before answering, simulate a neutral observer. Check your own biases.
meta.usage: When proposing the barnacle daemon, I simulated an impartial spectator: background process is overkill.

summary: All directives, explanations, and responses must be factored into the smallest coherent, independently understandable units possible

meta.heuristic: One logical change per commit. All files that must change together, no more.
meta.usage: We extracted push logic to a script, checked, committed — one unit.

summary: Prioritize the simplest and clearest articulation that meets the need, avoiding unnecessary complexity

meta.heuristic: If a 20-line TypeScript script can solve it, do not add a Python dependency.
meta.usage: The justfile is a facade: one-line delegations, not inline bash.

summary: Consciously prioritize deliberate analytical thinking for complex tasks, intuitive pattern-matching for trivial ones

meta.heuristic: Make small change → check → commit. If stuck >15 min: stop, revert, ask.
meta.usage: When the barnacle scan reported 16 findings, we used slow thinking to classify severity rather than reacting.

summary: Before generating complex outputs, first validate the core data or logic in a simple console format

meta.heuristic: Run reg-sync --all before building a UI. Validate the index before rendering the page.
meta.usage: We built scripts/reg-check.ts as a console validator before adding it to just check.

summary: Project lifecycle framework: Test, Automate, Scale, Evangelize

meta.heuristic: Test in scripts/lab. Automate in justfile. Scale with scripts. Evangelize in playbooks.
meta.usage: The unified registry started as a lab experiment, was automated via reg-sync, scaled to 6 registries, and documented in a playbook.

summary: When debugging performance issues, investigate data volume before refactoring code logic

meta.heuristic: The 683-line justfile was not slow because of complex logic. It was slow because it contained 683 lines of stuff.
meta.usage: We diagnosed the justfile bloat by counting lines per group, not by reading every recipe.

summary: Separate the active workbench from the filing cabinet. Explore freely, then clean up on completion.

meta.heuristic: scripts/lab/ is the workbench. src/ is the filing cabinet. Move only when proven.
meta.usage: We proved the PID file pattern in scripts/lab/pid-file.ts before building server-lifecycle.ts.

summary: If on attempt 3 of the same file without green check, stop and create a lab

meta.heuristic: Three failed attempts on production code = context window exhaustion. The lab prevents this.
meta.usage: The previous session edited server-lifecycle.ts three times directly, exhausted context, and produced 35 bundled commits. A lab would have absorbed the entropy.

summary: Use real data for layout experiments; mock data for API shape experiments

meta.heuristic: A table that looks good with 2 rows may wrap with 7. Only live data reveals this.
meta.usage: status-templates.ts used live service detection. ig-history.ts used mock data for format validation before API credentials were available.

summary: A lab-proven pattern should port to production in a single edit, passing check first time

meta.heuristic: If the port requires forward-fixes, the lab was not finished. The lab eliminates all unknowns.
meta.usage: Template E was proven in scripts/lab/status-template-e.ts before server-lifecycle.ts was edited. One edit, one commit, one green check.

summary: Every Gum display should have at most one border

meta.heuristic: Multiple nested borders create visual noise and brittle layout code. One border around data, titles and hints outside.
meta.usage: Template A-C failed because they used fixed-width boxes, nested cards, or multiple borders. Template E won with one border.

summary: The winning Gum display pattern: one border, dynamic width, title/hint outside, inline ANSI dots

meta.heuristic: Fixed --width fails with variable content. padEnd() math adapts. Inline ANSI provides per-row colour where Gum --foreground cannot.
meta.usage: Used for service status (server-lifecycle.ts), portfolio (portfolio.ts), alerts (alerts.ts), and IG history (ig-history.ts).

summary: A place where exploration mess is absorbed so production stays ordered

meta.heuristic: Direct editing under pressure produces entropy (broken commits, scope creep). The lab is the sink.
meta.usage: This session's four labs absorbed layout failures, API shape uncertainty, and alert edge cases before they touched production.

summary: All directives, explanations, and responses must be factored into the smallest coherent, independently understandable units possible.

meta.heuristic: One concern per commit. If a change touches N directories, break it into N commits.
meta.usage: The refactor required touching 5 files across 3 directories. I factored it into 3 separate PRs.

summary: I will always prioritize the simplest and clearest articulation that effectively meets the user's need, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

meta.heuristic: The justfile is a facade, not a workbench. Complex logic lives in scripts.
meta.usage: Instead of inlining the complex build logic in the justfile, I extracted it to scripts/build.ts.

summary: I will remain aware of the distinction between 'fast' (intuitive, pattern-matching) and 'slow' (deliberate, analytical) thinking, consciously prioritizing 'slow' thinking for all complex or high-stakes tasks to ensure rigor.

meta.heuristic: Use fast (pattern-matching) for trivial edits. Deliberate analysis for complex changes. If unsure, slow down.
meta.usage: The merge conflict looked simple, but I switched to slow thinking and found the real problem.

summary: Before generating complex outputs (e.g., UIs, visualizations), I will first output the core data or logic in a simple console format for rapid, low-friction validation.

meta.heuristic: Validate data before building UI. Run scripts in the lab before wiring to the dashboard.
meta.usage: Before building the portfolio chart, I validated the price data with scripts/get_price.ts.

summary: A project lifecycle framework: Test (validate the idea), Automate (build robust processes), Scale (ensure the solution handles complexity), and Evangelize (document and communicate).

meta.heuristic: Test the idea. Automate the process. Scale the system. Evangelize the pattern.
meta.usage: The alert system passed all tests, so I automated it with a just recipe and documented it in playbooks/.

summary: An operational heuristic for debugging performance issues that prioritizes investigating data volume over refactoring code logic. This protocol assumes that performance problems are more likely caused by unexpectedly large data volumes than by inefficient algorithms.

meta.heuristic: When debugging performance, check data volume before code logic.
meta.usage: The dashboard was slow. Before profiling, I checked the SQLite DB size and archive count.

summary: Formalizes a workflow for exploratory development ('tree-climbing') by separating the active 'workbench' (root folder) from the 'filing cabinet' (archive folders). This protocol maintains focus during exploration while ensuring clean project organization upon task completion.

meta.heuristic: Separate the workbench from the filing cabinet. Explore in scripts/lab/ before touching production.
meta.usage: I tested the new chart renderer in scripts/lab/chart-test.ts before moving it to src/server/views/.
